description: Engram's hooks are the entire mechanism by which memory reaches the model without the model asking for it, and the only thing that starts the server the MCP entry talks to. SessionStart runs two commands: ensure-server.sh, which brings up the local HTTP daemon on 127.0.0.1:7433 (idempotent, silent, and always exit 0 — a memory server that will not start makes a degraded session, not a broken one), and the primer. SessionStart fires on startup, resume, /clear, and after a compaction — every point where the agent's context is otherwise empty or thinner than a moment ago — and injects the session primer that names the memory tools and gives the agent a reason to call them. SubagentStart fires at every subagent spawn, including workflow-spawned agents that never came through an Agent tool call, and is the only channel that reaches all of them — SessionStart never fires for a subagent at all. It delivers a shorter primer whose one added point is that a subagent reports back through a summary, and summaries lose what was not written down. Bare stdout is silently discarded on that event, so it returns the hookSpecificOutput envelope; getting this wrong produces no error, just a primer that never arrives. PreCompact fires just before a compaction discards context; it records the event to telemetry and writes an instruction on bare stdout — the one channel measured to actually reach the model that writes the compaction summary — asking it to append a small delimited block of durable facts to that summary. PostCompact fires once that compaction has finished and carries the whole summary inline on stdin, so it reads back the delimited block PreCompact asked for and writes each durable fact as a session note tagged as harvester-authored, with no transcript read and no polling. UserPromptSubmit fires on every message the user sends and is the only place a fact the user states in passing can be caught — everything else in this system waits for the model to volunteer a tool call, and the M0 telemetry says it does not. It classifies the message sentence by sentence, stores only first-person statements and standing instructions (a question or an order to the assistant is neither), and asks the model to restate anything carrying a relative date or an unresolved pronoun. Sentence granularity is a privacy property as much as a precision one: the rest of the message never reaches disk. PreToolUse fires ahead of every file write and checkpoints the first write per session that targets Claude Code's file-based memory directory, deferring to engram_remember; it denies once with a reason and stays silent for the rest of the session, and [memory] precedence = off disarms it. PostToolUse on Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit fires after every file change and drops a tiny spool record under the Engram home's queue directory; the hook itself never opens the database (writes stay off the hot path), it only marks that a file changed so a later reindex knows what to look at. All of them exit 0 unless the home is uninitialized, in which case they are no-ops — a plugin installed but never `engram init`-ed does nothing rather than erroring.
